## p003 (sheet 2)
CHARACTER SHEET

LEFT SIDE OF SHEET   - ROLEPLAY-

CHARACTER INFO

In this section of the Character sheet you will fill in your name and some info you gain from your chosen Ancestry and Background.

LEVELS

Here you can track your Class Levels  (C.LVL)  and Party Level  (P.LVL).  Check page XX for more details.

EXPERTISE

These are used when making  ‘Checks’  outside of combat. There are 18 total Expertise, each with their own type of check. Each Expertise  is separated by what specific  ‘Main Stat’  it will add to the Check. You will increase specific Expertise by leveling up Classes and gaining  Party Levels. Check page XX for more details.

NON-COMBAT PASSIVE ABILITIES

These Passive Abilities will help you with specific bonuses outside combat. You will write in the Non-Combat Passive Ability you gain from  your Ancestry. You may write in another Non-Combat Passive from ANY class you have previously played as long as the Ability is unlocked.  You may do this again at Party Level 4 when you unlock another Non-Combat Passive Slot. Check page XX for more details.

BACKGROUND PASSIVE ABILITIES

When you gain a Background you will add your Background Abilities here. You will unlock new Abilities tied to your Background as your  Party Level increases. Check page XX for more details.

CLASS LEVELS

Here you can see how many Levels you need in specific Classes to unlock new Classes. You can also keep track of how many Levels you  have in each class.

RIGHT SIDE OF SHEET    -COMBAT-

HP / ENERGY / STATUS EFFECTS

During Combat you will track your MAX HP, how much Damage you have received, how much Energy you have used and any Status Effects  that you currently have.

CHARACTER STATS

You have 2 different types of stats, ‘Main Stats’ and ‘Bonus Stats’. These will increase based on many different elements. Main Stats are  used for Checks and Damage. Bonus Stats improve specific elements like mobility, protection, luck and Energy gain. Check page XX for  more details.

COMBAT PASSIVE ABILITIES

These Passive Abilities will help you with specific bonuses in combat. You will write in the Combat Passive Ability you gain from your  Ancestry. You may write in two other Combat Passives from ANY class you have previously played as long as the Ability is unlocked. You  may do this again at Party Level 8 when you unlock another Combat Passive Slot. Check page XX for more details.

EQUIPMENT

You may equip specific gear based on your  ‘Main Class’ . Each Class has a specific  ‘Main Hand’ ,  ‘Armor’ , and  ‘Off Hand’  they can equip.  There is no specific stipulations for equipping Accessories. Equipment is used to enhance Stats, increase damage, or give additional  effects inside and outside of combat.

INVENTORY

Keep track of any items obtained on your journey, each slot in your inventory can hold a stack of up to 5 of that item. Specific Items can  be used in or outside of combat.

SHARDS / GOLD

Shards are gained at specific Party Levels and may be given out by the GM when they deem it necessary. Shards have a number of uses  inside and outside of combat. Check page XX for more details. Here you may also track how much gold you have obtained on your journey.


## p004 (sheet 3)
ANCESTRIES CHARACTER CREATION

PARTY LEVEL STAT UPGRADE

Fill in the diamond pips when you gain a permanent Main Stat  from a  ‘Party Level’  Reward. You may only increase each Main  stat twice from Party Levels.

Before you can start playing the game you will need to create your  Character. While working on creating your Character work with the GM to  come up with a backstory that fits into their story. Below is the step by step  process of what you will need to do. You will utilize the next few sections of  the book: Ancestries, Backgrounds, and Classes.

PERMANENT STATS

Any time you see a stat inside a Square that means it is a  Permanent Stat increase. These Stats will not change.

On your Character sheet you will see multiple shapes to put in stat information.  These will collectively add up to create the total of the Stat they are under.

TEMPORARY STATS

Gear, Passive Abilities and other effects might give you Temporary  Stats as long as you are using them. These Stats may change.

STEP 2 - CHOOSE AN ANCESTRY

Each Ancestry will have a number of bonuses that you  add to your Character Sheet. On the left side of your  Character Sheet you will see a location to add in your  Ancestry’s Name, Language, and Vision. Under the  ‘Expertise’  Section add the corresponding Expertise from  your Ancestry as Permanent increases. Under the  ‘Non- Combat Passive Abilities’  Section add your Non-Combat  Ancestry Passive into the first Active slot.   (see Ex. 2)

On the right side of the Character Sheet add/subtract  Permanent Max HP, main Stats, and Bonus Stats. Under  the  ‘Combat Passive Abilities’  Section add your Combat  Ancestry Passive into the first Active slot.  (see Ex. 1)

STEP 3 - CHOOSE YOUR BACKGROUND

Each Background will have a few bonuses that you add to your  Character Sheet. On the left side of your Character Sheet under  the  ‘Expertise’  Section add the corresponding Expertise from your  Background as Permanent increases. You also gain Background  specific Passives that unlock as your Party Level increases. Add in  the corresponding abilities from your Background into those slots.  (see Ex. 3)

LEFT SIDE OF  CHARACTER SHEET

+ EXPERTISE + PASSIVE

RIGHT SIDE OF  CHARACTER SHEET

+ ITEMS / EQUIPMENT

On the right side of the sheet add any equipment or items gained  from your Background into your inventory.

STEP 4 - CHOOSE YOUR STARTING CLASS

There are six starter classes, each pertaining to a different type of  role. Choose Between Chemist, Gladiator, Ranger, Scholar, Soldier, and  Trickster. Once you have a Class selected this is now your  ‘Main Class’ .  Check Page XX for more information on Classes.

CHEMIST (HEALER)

GLADIATOR (TANK)

RANGER (RANGED DPS)

SCHOLAR (SPECIALIST)

Transfer over each  ‘Class Stat’  from the left side of your Class Sheet  to the corresponding Stat on your Character Sheet. Fill in each      with  the value shown. At the top of the Character sheet write in that X = 1.

SOLDIER (MELEE DPS)

TRICKSTER (SPECIALIST)

STEP 5 - CHOOSE YOUR STARTING GEAR

Each Character will get to choose a  ‘Starting Gear’  Bundle of their choice. Check page XX to choose your Starting Gear.


## p005 (sheet 3)
Next step is to select an Ancestry for your Character, this is the first step at fleshing out who your Character is before starting  your new Adventure. Read about their history, culture, and religion to see which Ancestry you think would fit the Character  you want to build. Each Ancestry is completely unique with various Passive Abilities and stats that will help define who you  are. Once selected, gain the following from your Ancestry:

LEFT SIDE OF THE CHARACTER SHEET (EX. 2)

Add your Ancestry name, known languages, and vision to the top section on the left side of your  ‘Character Sheet’ .

Add the Permanent ‘Expertise’ gained from your Ancestry to the      in the next section down on the left side of the ‘Character  Sheet’. Write in the ‘Non-Combat Passive’ gained from your ‘Ancestry’ into the top slot in the next section ‘Non-Combat Passive  Abilities’.

RIGHT SIDE OF THE CHARACTER SHEET (EX. 1)

Add the Permanent ‘MAX HP’ gained from your Ancestry into the     on ‘MAX HP’ at the top section of the right side of  your ‘Character Sheet’.

Add the 2 Permanent ‘Main Stats’ gained from your Ancestry into the      on the corresponding ‘Main Stats’ in the next  section  called ‘Character Stats’ on the right side of your ‘Character Sheet’. (You will always gain 1 positive Stat and 1 negative Stat.)

Add the Permanent ‘Bonus Stat’ gained from your Ancestry into the      on the corresponding ‘Bonus Stat’ in the ‘Character  Stats’ section.  Write in the ‘Combat Passive’ gained from your ‘Ancestry’ into the top slot in the next section ‘Combat Passive Abilities’.

HYBRID ANCESTRIES

Talk with your GM if you are interested in creating a hybrid Ancestry. If the GM allows it you may select up to 2 Ancestries  if you feel that would be applicable to your Character. When Selecting 2 Ancestries, you will have to follow some rules:

Each time you are choosing bonuses you may only select 1 choice per bonus. For example; if you are making a hybrid  between the Nethander and the Uhhranti you may only choose 1 language (besides common), 1 type of vision, Expertise  bonuses from 1 of the Ancestries, 1 positive Main Stat, 1 negative Main Stat, 1 Bonus Stat, 1 non-Combat Passive, and  1 Combat Passive between the 2 Ancestries.  You must choose the lower ‘MAX HP’ bonus between the 2 Ancestries.

## p030 (sheet 16)
BACKGROUNDS

CHOOSE YOUR

BACKGROUND

After selecting the Ancestry for your character you will then select a Background.  Selecting a background helps determine what your character was like before starting  your new Adventure. Each background is completely unique with various abilities  that will come in handy to you and your Party. Once a Background is selected, gain  the following:

Gain 2 permanent points in specific Expertise.

Add the  ‘Starting Items’  from your Background to your Inventory.

Each Background will have abilities that unlock as your Party Levels up. You  unlock a Background ability at Party Level 0, 3, 6, and 9. These abilities will be  added to your  ‘Character Sheet’  in the section that looks like the graphic below:

You may select up to 2 Backgrounds if you feel that would be applicable to your  Character. When Selecting 2 Backgrounds, you will have to make a few choices:

When you are gaining Permanent  ‘Expertise’  from a background you may only  choose 1 of your chosen Background’s Expertise rewards.

When gaining  ‘Starting Items’  from a Background, you may only choose 1 of the  chosen Background’s Starting Items Rewards.

Look at the  ‘Background Abilities’  of each Background you have chosen. In the Title  Section of the Background Ability on your Character sheet add both Background  names. For each section where you unlock an Ability (Party Level 0, 3, 6, and 9) you  must choose 1 Ability from 1 Background for each of those sections and add them to  your sheet now. For example, If you chose the Barbarian & Psychologist Backgrounds:  you have to choose between one of their Level 0 Abilities, add it to the Character  sheet. Choose between 1 of their Level 3 Abilities, add it to the Character sheet, and  so on. Check page XX for more information about selecting 2 Backgrounds.

When you select a Background, you will gain Expertise, Items, and Abilities that will  level up with your Party Level. If you look at the  ‘Blacksmith’  Background on the next  page, you will see a variety of unlocks you get when selecting it.

Add a Permanent  +2 Bonus  to your  Crafting Expertise  on your Character Sheet.

Add a  Blacksmith’s Writ  and a  (+1 Damage) Weapon  of your choice added to  your Inventory.

Add the Blacksmith’s  Background Abilities  to your Character sheet.

Your Background will unlock Abilities at Party Level: 0, 3, 6, & 9. For example; the  Blacksmith  will be able to craft better weapons the higher your Party Level is.

The difficulty  of the  ‘Mind’  Check is at the discretion of the GM. Grifter:  Grifting is the act of getting money or goods from someone  through deceit, fraud, or a confidence game. The difficulty of the  ‘Deception’  Check is at the discretion of the GM.

## p045 (sheet 23)
FLESH OUT YOUR BACKGROUND:

Use your Selected Background(s) to help flesh out your Character. This will be a defining feature of  your Character as you progress through this new Journey. If you are selecting 2 Backgrounds take into  consideration how each one has built your Character. You can utilize this to combine 2 Backgrounds to  create a new one that might not be in the current list of Backgrounds. Below are a few examples of how  you can combine Backgrounds to better fit your Character.

You found a love of smithing at an early age and picked up on it quickly. You found that devoting yourself  to only learning to craft weapons or only craft armor was too limiting. You dabbled in both Blacksmithing  and Armorsmithing never mastering either. you would want to choose the Blacksmith and Armorsmith  background, mixing and matching their Rewards and Abilities.

You joined the military as soon as you were allowed to and fought in a war before heading back to your  home town. Once back, you took your military knowledge and put it to good use as a royal guard for the  local king. If this was your back story, you would want to choose the Military and Guard background,  mixing and matching their Rewards and Abilities.

Lets say you wanted your Character to have been a Pirate, you could select the Sailor Background. If  you feel the Sailor Background doesn’t have enough of that Piratey feel to it, you could instead select  the Sailor Background and the Swindler or Rogue Background. Mix and match the Abilities and stats  from the 2 Backgrounds to create the Pirate that suites your Character best.

## p046 (sheet 24)
CLASSES

As a Fragment you are capable of accessing and harnessing the power of memories that lay dorment inside the  ‘Source’ .  Unlike the common man, this power gives you the ability to utilize specialties from across multiple universes. The more you  use this connection to the Source the stronger your tether to it becomes, allowing you to gain access to even more memories.  Being a Fragment you can swap between these specialties and retain the knowledge you learn from one specialty and use  it to enhance another.

At the start of your Adventure you will choose 1 Starter Class: Chemist, Gladiator, Ranger, Scholar, Soldier, or Trickster.  Add  the MAX HP and Stats on your  ‘Main Class’  Sheet to your  ‘Character Sheet’ . Check the top left section of the Class Sheet  and add the numbers in the      on your Class Sheet to the corresponding MAX HP or Stat in the      on your Character Sheet.  These will get added to your total for that Stat.

Once you reach Class Level 10 with one of the Starter Classes you will gain acess to the next tier of Classes. Once you gain  access to new Classes you can swap to a new  ‘Main Class’ . When swapping to a new Main Class, any of your previous  Classes you have played can be used as a  ‘Sub Class’ . You can use any of the Abilities on the Right side of the Sub Class but  no longer have access to the left side of the sheet. You can overlay your sheets like the example below to make this easier.  Make sure you change your     Stats to what your current Main Class gives you and don’t forget you can also write in ANY  unlocked passive abilities from previous classes you have played onto your Character Sheet.

## p049 (sheet 25)
LEFT SIDE OF CLASS SHEET

LEFT SIDE OF SHEET

CLASS INFO

Here you will find the Icon and name of your class followed by the Prerequisites and what classes playing this class can unlock. There are  also icons that indicate the type of roll the Class will play in battle. You will also see a box that says  ‘X=’ , X is often a modifier for damage  or other effects and it Increases as your Party Level goes up. X starts at 1.

STATS

Add the MAX HP and Stats on your Main  ‘Class Sheet’  to your  ‘Character Sheet’ . Add the numbers in the     on your Class Sheet to the  corresponding MAX HP or Stat in the      on your Character Sheet. These will get added to your total for that Stat.

ULTIMATE ABILITY

Each Class has a unique  ‘Ultimate’  Ability, these are specific Abilities only usable in combat. You must fill each      to use the Ultimate Ability,  to fill a     will require you to do specific Actions during Combat. These requirements are listed below the Ultimate Ability. Once you have  filled all 10      you can use the Ultimate Ability any time, during Combat, as long as you aren’t interrupting an Action. Using an Ultimate  Ability is considered a  ‘Reaction’ .

COMBAT MODIFIERS

This section will list how each Class will function in Combat. Make sure you read through this section thoroughly and how you can utilize  these modifiers with the Class.

STARS

As you unlock new Abilities you will gain  ‘Stars’  that represent how many Abilities you have unlocked. Each time you gain a Star from  unlocking an Ability on the ‘Right Side’ of the sheet fill in 1 Star on EACH Expertise and  ‘Locked Passives’  Section. Once something has all  of its Stars filled, it becomes unlock and you will gain a bonus reward.

EXPERTISE

Add a permanent increase to a specific Expertise once it has all of it’s Stars filled in.

EQUIPMENT

This section will tell you what you are capable of equipping in your  ‘Main Hand’ ,  ‘Armor’ , and  ‘Off Hand’ . These are strict requirements that  must be followed so keep an eye on what gear you have equipped when Changing classes because you might need new gear. If no gear  is equipped you are always considered to have a base version of your required gear that gives no bonus.

RIGHT SIDE OF SHEET

PASSIVES

Each class starts with a  ‘Non-Combat’  and  ‘Combat’  Passive unlocked. If it is your  ‘Main Class’  you may use these passives without adding  them to your Character Sheet. You will gain an additional Combat Passive & a Permanent increase to a specific Stat once you have learned  all the Abilities on the Class Sheet (Represented by the number of Stars needed to unlock.) You may use any Unlocked Passive Abilities  from Classes you have Previously Played by adding them to available  ‘Passive’  Slots on your Character Sheet.

RIGHT SIDE OF CLASS SHEET

CLASS LEVEL

Each Class can gain a total of 20  ‘Class Levels’ . When your GM awards you a Class Level you will fill in one      on a Locked Ability, or the      if all other      are filled in for the Ability. Once all     and       are filled in that Ability is unlocked. In the top right corner of the sheet is a  section called  ‘Class Level’  where you can write in your current level.

MAIN ACTIONS

During Combat you will have a number of  ‘Main Actions’  you can utilize. You may only use 1 Main Action per round unless otherwise  specified.  ( go to page XX for more information).

SUPPORT ACTIONS

During Combat you will have a number of  ‘Support Actions’  you can utilize. You may only use 1 Support Action per round unless otherwise  specified or if you do not use a  ‘Move Action’ .  ( go to page XX for more information).

REACTIONS

During Combat you will have a number of  ‘Reactions’  you can utilize. Reactions have specific  ‘Conditions’  that must be followed to be  used. These Abilities can be used  ‘Off Turn’  as long as you still follow the condition for use.  ( go to page XX for more information).

## p051 (sheet 26)
Chemists aren’t as advanced as an Alchemist but they can  use Chemisty to craft potions from found ingredients. Their  resourcefulness and quick crafting make them a great addition  to a Party as a field medic. With their crafting abilities and quick  hands they are capable of creating potions and tossing them  across the battlefield with precision to those in need of healing.

ENHANCED CHEMISTRY   COMBAT MODIFIER

Chemist’s have a  ‘Non-Combat’  Passive called  ‘Chemistry’  that can  be used to gather ingredients and craft a variety of Items using the  found ingredients. While Chemist is your  ‘Main Class’  Enhanced  Chemisty increases how many ingredients you find when using  the Passive Ability. The Items created using this Ability are placed  in your inventory until used. The Chemist’s  ‘Throwing’  Abilities  require you to spend Items from your Inventory when used.  Though you are a Chemist you can dabble in some  ‘Basic  Alchemy’ . When using one of your  ‘Throwing’  Abilities, roll a D6  and potentially gain an effect. If you roll 1-3 gain nothing, roll 4-5  increase HP restored or +INT Damage dealt depending on the  item used, or roll a 6 do not spend the Item used for the Ability.

EXPERTISE  SPECIALTIES

Crafting Expertise   - Being a Chemist teaches you how to  be more efficient when it comes to crafting.  After learning 2  Abilities you will permanently increase your Crafting Expertise.  Throw/Catch Expertise   - After throwing so many Items across  the battlefield you enhance your precision when it comes to  throwing.  After learning 4 Abilities you will permanently increase  your Throw/Catch Expertise.

EQUIPMENT  REQUIREMENTS

Main Hand [Ranged (Piercing)]   - Capable of equipping  Ranged (Piercing) Weapons, starts with a Pistol with no bonus.

Armor [Medium]   - Capable of equipping Medium Armor, starts  with basic medium armor with no bonus.

Off Hand [Dagger]  - Capable of equipping Daggers in their Off  Hand for Melee Attacks. Starts with a basic Dagger with no bonus.

PASSIVE  ABILITIES

Chemistry   - Once per ‘Long Rest’, outside of Combat, you can  gather up ingredients you find and craft a variety of Items.  Throw Proficiency   - Typically you may only use Items at a  Range of 1 unless otherwise specified but using this Passive  allows you to Throw Items from your Inventory at a Range of 10.  Mixologist  - Once you have Mastered Chemist by learning all  their Abilities gain access to the  ‘Mixologist’  passive. Items gain  +INT Damage dealt and HP Restored when spending Items from  your Inventory.

CHEMIST

STARTER CLASS

ABILITIES  COMBAT

INT

MAIN STAT:

The Chemist’s primary goal in Combat is to keep the party  alive by throwing potions at their allies.They are also capable  of crafting poison bombs and come armed with a Piercing  (Ranged) Weapon. They can utilize both to increase the DPS of  the Party when need be. Unlike other healers that typically utilize  ‘Magic’  for healing, the Chemist uses purely physical Items. This  comes with a few benefits, like allowing the Chemist to  ‘Chain’  into Restorative Abilities and Items restore a set amount of HP.

PHYSICAL RANGED HEALER

PREREQUISITES:

N/A

UNLOCKS:

All Tier 1 Classes   [10 Levels]  |   Alchemist   [15 Levels]

The Items created using this Ability are placed  in your inventory until used. The Chemist’s ‘Throwing’ Abilities  require you to spend Items from your Inventory when used.  Though you are a Chemist you can dabble in some ‘Basic  Alchemy’. When using one of your ‘Throwing’ Abilities, roll a D6  and potentially gain an effect. If you roll 1-3 gain nothing, roll 4-5  increase HP restored or +INT Damage dealt depending on the  item used, or roll a 6 do not spend the Item used for the Ability.

EXPERTISE  SPECIALTIES

Crafting Expertise   - Being a Chemist teaches you how to  be more efficient when it comes to crafting.  After learning 2  Abilities you will permanently increase your Crafting Expertise.  Throw/Catch Expertise   - After throwing so many Items across  the battlefield you enhance your precision when it comes to  throwing.  After learning 4 Abilities you will permanently increase  your Throw/Catch Expertise.

EQUIPMENT   REQUIREMENTS

Main Hand [Bludgeoning]   - Capable of equipping Bludgeoning  Weapons, starts with a basic Hammer with no bonus.

Armor [Light Armor]   - Capable of equipping Light Armor, starts  with basic Light Armor with no bonus.

Off Hand [Pistol/Crossbow]   - Capable of equipping Pistols or  1-handed crossbows in their Off Hand. Starts with no bonus.

PASSIVE   ABILITIES

Chemistry   - Once per ‘Long Rest’, outside of Combat, you can  gather up ingredients you find and craft a variety of Items.  Throw Proficiency   - Typically you may only use Items at a  Range of 1 unless otherwise specified but using this Passive  allows you to Throw Items from your Inventory at a Range of 10.  Mixologist   - Once you have Mastered Chemist by learning all  their Abilities gain access to the ‘Mixologist’ passive. Items gain  +INT Damage dealt and HP Restored when spending Items from  your Inventory.

TRICKSTER

## p078 (sheet 40)
> [NO EMBEDDED TEXT — full-page art/diagram/cover. Needs vision: assets/handbook_scan/p078.avif]

## p079 (sheet 40)
Chemists aren’t as advanced as an Alchemist but they can  use Chemisty to craft potions from found ingredients. Their  resourcefulness and quick crafting make them a great addition  to a Party as a field medic. With their crafting abilities and quick  hands they are capable of creating potions and tossing them  across the battlefield with precision to those in need of healing.

CHANGE FATE   COMBAT MODIFIER

Chemist’s have a ‘Non-Combat’ Passive that can be used to  gather ingredients and craft a variety of Items using the found  ingredients. While Chemist is your ‘Main Class’ Enhanced  Chemisty increases how many ingredients you find when using  the Passive Ability. The Items created using this Ability are placed  in your inventory until used. The Chemist’s ‘Throwing’ Abilities  require you to spend Items from your Inventory when used.  Though you are a Chemist you can dabble in some ‘Basic  Alchemy’. When using one of your ‘Throwing’ Abilities, roll a D6  and potentially gain an effect. If you roll 1-3 gain nothing, roll 4-5  increase HP restored or +INT Damage dealt depending on the  item used, or roll a 6 do not spend the Item used for the Ability.

EXPERTISE  SPECIALTIES

Crafting Expertise   - Being a Chemist teaches you how to  be more efficient when it comes to crafting.  After learning 2  Abilities you will permanently increase your Crafting Expertise.  Throw/Catch Expertise   - After throwing so many Items across  the battlefield you enhance your precision when it comes to  throwing.  After learning 4 Abilities you will permanently increase  your Throw/Catch Expertise.

EQUIPMENT   REQUIREMENTS

Main Hand [Focus]   - Capable of equipping Focus Weapons,  starts with a basic Tome with no bonus.

Armor [Light Armor]   - Capable of equipping Light Armor, starts  with basic Light Armor with no bonus.

Off Hand [Tome]  - Capable of equipping Tomes in their Off  Hand. Starts with a basic Tome with no bonus.

PASSIVE   ABILITIES

Chemistry   - Once per ‘Long Rest’, outside of Combat, you can  gather up ingredients you find and craft a variety of Items.  Throw Proficiency   - Typically you may only use Items at a  Range of 1 unless otherwise specified but using this Passive  allows you to Throw Items from your Inventory at a Range of 10.  Mixologist   - Once you have Mastered Chemist by learning all  their Abilities gain access to the ‘Mixologist’ passive. Items gain  +INT Damage dealt and HP Restored when spending Items from  your Inventory.

CHRONOMANCER

TIER 2 CLASS

ABILITIES   COMBAT

MND

MAIN STAT:

The Chemist’s primary goal in Combat is to keep the party  alive by throwing potions at their allies.They are also capable  of crafting poison bombs and come armed with a Piercing  (Ranged) Weapon. They can utilize both to increase the DPS of  the Party when need be. Unlike other healers that typically utilize  ‘Magic’  for healing, the Chemist uses purely physical Items. This  comes with a few benefits, like allowing the Chemist to  ‘Chain’  into Restorative Abilities and Items restore a set amount of HP.

MAGIC RANGED SUPPORT

SABOTEUR

PREREQUISITES:

Priest  - Level: 10

UNLOCKS:

Invoker  [10 Levels]  |   Judge   [10 Levels]

## p097 (sheet 49)
Chemists aren’t as advanced as an Alchemist but they can  use Chemisty to craft potions from found ingredients. Their  resourcefulness and quick crafting make them a great addition  to a Party as a field medic. With their crafting abilities and quick  hands they are capable of creating potions and tossing them  across the battlefield with precision to those in need of healing.

COMMUNION   COMBAT MODIFIER

Chemist’s have a ‘Non-Combat’ Passive that can be used to  gather ingredients and craft a variety of Items using the found  ingredients. While Chemist is your ‘Main Class’ Enhanced  Chemisty increases how many ingredients you find when using  the Passive Ability. The Items created using this Ability are placed  in your inventory until used. The Chemist’s ‘Throwing’ Abilities  require you to spend Items from your Inventory when used.  Though you are a Chemist you can dabble in some ‘Basic  Alchemy’. When using one of your ‘Throwing’ Abilities, roll a D6  and potentially gain an effect. If you roll 1-3 gain nothing, roll 4-5  increase HP restored or +INT Damage dealt depending on the  item used, or roll a 6 do not spend the Item used for the Ability.

EXPERTISE  SPECIALTIES

Crafting Expertise   - Being a Chemist teaches you how to  be more efficient when it comes to crafting.  After learning 2  Abilities you will permanently increase your Crafting Expertise.  Throw/Catch Expertise   - After throwing so many Items across  the battlefield you enhance your precision when it comes to  throwing.  After learning 4 Abilities you will permanently increase  your Throw/Catch Expertise.

EQUIPMENT   REQUIREMENTS

Main Hand [Slashing/Bludgeoning]   - Capable of equipping  Slashing or Bludgeoning Weapons, starts with a Sword with no bonus.

Armor [Heavy]   - Capable of equipping Heavy Armor, starts with  basic Heavy Armor with no bonus.

Off Hand [Shield]   - Capable of equipping Shields in their Off  Hand. Starts with a basic Shield with no bonus.

PASSIVE   ABILITIES

Chemistry   - Once per ‘Long Rest’, outside of Combat, you can  gather up ingredients you find and craft a variety of Items.  Throw Proficiency   - Typically you may only use Items at a  Range of 1 unless otherwise specified but using this Passive  allows you to Throw Items from your Inventory at a Range of 10.  Mixologist   - Once you have Mastered Chemist by learning all  their Abilities gain access to the ‘Mixologist’ passive. Items gain  +INT Damage dealt and HP Restored when spending Items from  your Inventory.

PALADIN
